clue.text: Writer damages toecap

indicators.note: damages says the letters of the following word are knocked out of shape and rearranged

explanation.surface: An author ruins the steel toe of a boot.
explanation.definitionFit: Truman Capote was the American author of In Cold Blood and Breakfast at Tiffany's.

clue.text: One is better out of it

definitions.text: One is better out of it

parts.words: One is better out of it
parts.note: reads like advice to leave a bad situation, but means a recovered patient has come out of an illness

explanation.walkthrough: 'Better' means recovered from illness, not superior: a person who is better is out of their ailment.
explanation.definitionFit: Being better after an illness means one has emerged from a state of ill health.

clue.text: Smart fuels could be of benefit

parts.note: U is the crossword letter for upper-class or posh, hence smart

indicators.note: could be suggests the following word might be some other arrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: Clever new fuels might prove advantageous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smart' looks like an adjective on fuels, but gives U (upper-class); 'could be' rearranges FUELS into SEFUL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something helpful or practical is of benefit, the meaning of the adjective.

clue.text: Flamboyant style of love on board

indicators.note: on, as in being on board a vessel, places the love letter inside the ship

parts.note: board stands for a ship, as in the phrase on board; a barque is a sailing ship
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: An ornate fashion of romance aboard ship.
explanation.walkthrough: A barque is a three-masted sailing ship; being 'on board' it puts O inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Baroque is the ornate, highly decorated style of seventeenth-century European art and music.

clue.text: Poet on "The Ancient Mariner"

parts.note: Alexander Pope was the eighteenth-century English poet
ye is an old form of the word the, as in Ye Olde Tea Shoppe

explanation.surface: A poet comments on Coleridge's famous Rime of the Ancient Mariner.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface invokes Coleridge's poem, but 'The Ancient' gives archaic YE, the old spelling of 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: Popeye is the cartoon sailor, so a mariner by trade.

clue.text: Manner of much of 5's depiction of opposites?

definitions.meaning: much of 5 is the poet Pope, who wrote chiefly in rhyming couplets, so his depictions came in lines of poetry
in mathematics, values that undo each other, such as reciprocals

explanation.walkthrough: 'Much of 5' is POPEYE cut short, the poet Pope, whose work was in verse; split as IN VERSES it describes his manner.
explanation.definitionFit: In logic and maths, inverses are things turned the other way round, hence opposites.

clue.text: A semi built in new land is what women go for

indicators.note: in places the rebuilt semi within the rearranged land
new indicates the following word appears in a fresh arrangement
built suggests the letters of a semi are constructed into a new form

explanation.surface: Women flock to a semi-detached house erected in a fresh territory.
explanation.walkthrough: Here 'built' and 'new' are separate anagram signals: the house letters are rebuilt and set within a reshuffled land, and 'what women go for' is a wry definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A man who charms and attracts women is a womaniser, the sort women supposedly fall for.

clue.text: Treading on them shows contempt from start to finish

indicators.note: from start to finish says a letter at the beginning of the word is carried to the end

parts.note: scorn is disdain or contempt

explanation.surface: Stepping on them signals disdain all the way through.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'from start to finish' looks like 'throughout', but it moves the first S of SCORN to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Treading on someone's corns means offending them, so the hard foot lumps are what one treads on.

clue.text: Historic work journal?

parts.note: reads as a log of one's daily tasks, but means an ancient scriptural text named after a patriarch

explanation.walkthrough: 'Journal' as a record of one's work suggests a book of jobs; the real answer is the ancient Old Testament book.
explanation.definitionFit: The Book of Job is an ancient work of the Hebrew Bible, punningly a record of a job.

clue.text: Control of leading character in soap

definitions.meaning: a handle used to operate machinery
William ... founded ... Brothers, the soap company behind Sunlight soap

explanation.walkthrough: 'Soap' suggests a television soap opera, but means actual soap: Lever Brothers made Sunlight soap.
explanation.definitionFit: A lever is a handle that controls a mechanism, and Lever is the soap-making family name.

clue.text: Darkness is almost upon us

indicators.note: almost says the word falls short by its final letter

parts.note: night is the time of darkness

explanation.surface: Night is very nearly here.
explanation.definitionFit: Something close at hand is nigh, meaning near or imminent.

clue.text: Withdraw treatment for a leper

indicators.note: treatment for says the following letters are worked on and rearranged

explanation.surface: Retreat from offering care to someone with leprosy.
explanation.definitionFit: To repeal a law is to revoke or withdraw it formally.

clue.text: Everything is misrep-resented in revues

indicators.note: misrep-resented, itself a broken word, says the letters are shown wrongly arranged

explanation.surface: Every topic gets distorted in satirical theatre shows.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen in 'misrep-resented' is a joke mirroring the anagram it signals.
explanation.definitionFit: The universe is the whole of existence, all things there are.

clue.text: Certain time before cancellation …

indicators.note: before puts the time period ahead of the word for certain

parts.note: an era is a period of time
sure means certain

explanation.surface: A definite deadline precedes a cancellation.
explanation.definitionFit: An erasure is a rubbing-out or deletion, a cancellation of what was written.

clue.text: Dreamy perhaps before nine, but it sets later

indicators.note: before places the rearranged letters ahead of the nine
perhaps hints the preceding word might be in some other order

parts.note: IX is nine in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A drowsy person, maybe, before nine o'clock, though bedtime comes later.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it sets later' suggests the sun, but means concrete; 'perhaps' turns DREAMY into READYM.
explanation.definitionFit: Ready-mix concrete is delivered wet and hardens, or sets, after pouring.

clue.text: Proportion of fire appliances cut

indicators.note: Proportion of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some of the fire engines were cut back.
explanation.definitionFit: To reap is to cut a crop such as corn at harvest.

clue.text: … so there's time for what's left

parts.note: taken as written; that the answer also runs across there's time is a coincidence, since T is the abbreviation of time in a charade

explanation.surface: So there is still some time for the remainder.
explanation.definitionFit: The rest is the remainder, whatever is left over.

clue.text: One may provide a record in outbreak of terror

definitions.text: One may provide a record in outbreak of terror

indicators.note: in places the record inside the scattered letters
outbreak of says the letters of the next word burst out into a new order

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A journalist may supply an account during an eruption of fear.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: a journalist provides a record of events when terror breaks out.
explanation.definitionFit: A reporter is a journalist who records events, often during crises.

clue.text: Score up above is inadequate

indicators.note: up, read as up in, puts the score among the heavens

parts.note: the sky is what is up above
to etch is to score or cut a mark into a surface

explanation.surface: A musical score high above the stage is found wanting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Score' suggests music, but means to scratch a line, and the sky is what lies up above.
explanation.definitionFit: Sketchy describes something incomplete or lacking detail, hence inadequate.

clue.text: To confront wolves, say, could save one's skin

parts.note: to face something is to confront it
wolves are an example of animals that hunt in a pack

explanation.surface: Standing up to a pack of wolves might be how you survive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'save one's skin' sounds like escaping danger, but a cosmetic mask literally tends the skin.
explanation.definitionFit: A face pack is a cosmetic paste applied to cleanse and protect the facial skin.

clue.text: Politician in Ireland, once British

indicators.note: in places the politician inside the name for Ireland

parts.note: Eire is the Irish-language name for Ireland
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A member of parliament in Ireland, which was formerly ruled by Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: The British Empire once spanned much of the world; an empire that was British is now gone.

clue.text: Fame of salesman with outback transport

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative
a ute is an Australian utility pickup vehicle, used in the outback

explanation.surface: The renown of a travelling salesman with his Australian pickup truck.
explanation.definitionFit: Repute is reputation or renown, a synonym of fame.

clue.text: Electric terminals removed and carelessly left

indicators.note: carelessly says the remaining letters are thrown together in a new order
terminals removed says the end letters of the word are stripped away

explanation.surface: Electric terminals were taken out and left lying about without care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terminals removed' leaves LECTRI from ELECTRIC, which 'carelessly' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Relict is an old word for something left behind or surviving, as a widow is left.

clue.text: More perhaps wrestling with maths — but there's nothing in it

indicators.note: in places the zero inside the rearranged letters
wrestling with suggests the letters of the next word are grappled into a new order

parts.note: O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone struggling with arithmetic finds there is nothing to it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'More' is not a comparative: it is Sir Thomas More, the Tudor statesman.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Thomas More, author of Utopia, had the first name Thomas, so More is an example.

clue.text: Young maiden Falstaff's follower takes to the local

parts.note: Nym is one of Falstaff's companions in Shakespeare's Merry Wives of Windsor and Henry V
PH is the abbreviation for public house, a British pub, often called the local

explanation.surface: A young girl tags along with a Shakespearean rogue to the neighbourhood pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A nymph is a beautiful young woman, from the maiden nature spirits of myth.

clue.text: Peaceful corner for spirited company?

definitions.meaning: a quiet room where all is calm
a room in a great house where spirits and cordials were distilled

explanation.walkthrough: 'spirited company' suggests lively guests, but means distilled liquor.
explanation.definitionFit: A stillroom was a household room for distilling, and read literally it is a quiet room.

clue.text: Clerical award for dubious merit?

indicators.note: dubious says the following word is in a questionable, altered order

explanation.surface: A church honour given for questionable worth.
explanation.definitionFit: A mitre is the headdress conferred on a bishop, so an ecclesiastical honour.

clue.text: Time 18 took year off as a writer

parts.note: 18 down is a reporter, and a hack is a journalist

indicators.note: off indicates the letters of the word are thrown out of their order

explanation.surface: A journalist took a year off to become an author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'took year off' looks like a sabbatical, but 'off' rearranges YEAR into ERAY.
explanation.definitionFit: William Makepeace Thackeray was the Victorian novelist who wrote Vanity Fair.
